abstract: Leveraging the power of multimodal imaging relies on accurate coregistration of yet fundamentally different modalities. Reliable cell-to-cell correspondence is especially challenging as consecutive tissue sections do not necessarily contain identical cells or cellular structures. Here we present MeXalign, a segmentation-mask-based coregistration pipeline designed to integrate multimodal images acquired sequentially from the same specimen at single-cell resolution. Single-cell segmentation masks provide a modality-independent representation of cellular morphology and spatial organization. MeXalign was tested based on the two platforms, laser ablation inductively coupled plasma time-of-flight mass spectrometry (LA-ICP-TOFMS) and immunofluorescence (IF) microscopy. As a prerequisite, each modality integrates membrane and/or nucleus labels for accurate segmentation. The added value of MeXalign was highlighted for imaging of cell models deposited on glass slides and tissue sections. The performance of coregistration was validated on cytospins, murine tumor and human skin samples. A dedicated scoring system was introduced allowing to assess the quality of image coregistration. The robustness towards under-segmentation and downstream image analysis was evaluated on LA-ICP-TOFMS with and without coregistration, investigating metal drug uptake, barcoding and cellular phenotyping. A showcase study on cancer cells exposed to nanoparticles proved the accuracy, as the nanoparticle distribution was preserved at a subcellular level when using MeXalign. While all examples show the overall improved quality of segmentation, other benefits of complementary labelings can be anticipated, especially for cellular features unique to one modality.
